'''Ludwig Otto Hesse''' (22 April 1811 &ndash; 4 August 1874) was a German [[mathematician]]. Hesse was born in [[Königsberg]], [[Kingdom of Prussia|Prussia]], and died in [[Munich]], [[Kingdom of Bavaria|Bavaria]]. He worked mainly on [[algebraic invariant]]s, and [[geometry]]. The [[Hessian matrix]], the [[Hesse normal form]], the [[Hesse configuration]], the [[Hessian group]], [[Hessian pair]]s,  [[Hesse's theorem]], [[Hesse pencil]], and the [[Hesse transfer principle]]<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=XTYDCAAAQBAJ&pg=PA111|title=Mathematics of the 19th Century: Geometry, Analytic Function Theory|editor-last=Kolmogorov|editor-first=Andrei N.|editor-link=Andrey Kolmogorov|editor-last2=Yushkevich|editor-first2=Adolf-Andrei P.|editor-link2=Adolph P. Yushkevich|year=2012|publisher=Birkhäuser|isbn=9783034891738|language=en|page=111}}</ref> are named after him. Many of Hesse's research findings were presented for the first time in ''[[Crelle's Journal]]'' or Hesse's textbooks.<ref>[[MacTutor History of Mathematics archive]] and [[Complete Dictionary of Scientific Biography]]</ref>

==Life==
Hesse was born in Königsberg (today [[Kaliningrad]]) as the son of Johann Gottlieb Hesse, a businessman and brewery owner and his wife Anna Karoline Reiter (1788–1865). He studied in his hometown at the [[University of Königsberg|Albertina]] under [[Carl Gustav Jacob Jacobi]]. Among his teachers were count [[Friedrich Wilhelm Bessel]] and [[Friedrich Julius Richelot]]. He earned his doctorate in 1840 at the [[University of Königsberg]] with the dissertation ''De octo punctis intersectionis trium superficium secundi ordinis''. In 1841, Hesse completed his [[habilitation]] thesis. In the same year he married Sophie Marie Emilie Dulk, the daughter of pharmacists and chemistry professor [[Friedrich Philipp Dulk]] (1788–1852). The couple had a son and five daughters. Hesse taught for some time physics and chemistry at the Vocational School in Königsberg and lectured at the Albertina. In 1845 he was appointed associate professor in Königsberg. In 1855 he moved to Halle and in 1856 to Heidelberg until 1868, when he finally moved to [[Munich]] to the newly established [[Technical University of Munich|Polytechnic School]]. In 1869 he joined the [[Bavarian Academy of Sciences]].

His doctoral students include [[Olaus Henrici]], [[Gustav Kirchhoff]], [[Jacob Lüroth]], [[Christian Gustav Adolph Mayer|Adolph Mayer]], [[Carl Neumann]], [[Max Noether]], [[Ernst Schröder (mathematician)|Ernst Schröder]], and [[Heinrich Martin Weber]].<ref name="otto">{{MathGenealogy|id=46967|title=Otto Hesse}}</ref>

==Works==
* ''Vorlesungen über analytische Geometrie des Raumes.'' (Lectures on analytic geometry of space) Leipzig (3. A. 1876) ([https://archive.org/details/vorlesungenbera03hessgoog Internet Archive])
* ''Vorlesungen aus der analytischen Geometrie der geraden Linie, des Punktes und des Kreises.'' (Lectures from the analytical geometry of the straight line, the point and the circle) Leipzig (1881). Hrsg. A. Gundelfinger ([https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_at6qA3g2YDwC Internet Archive])
* ''Die Determinanten elementar behandelt.'' (Determinants elementary treated) Leipzig (2. A. 1872) ([http://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/dms/load/img/?PID=PPN373460147 Göttinger Digitalisierungszentrum])
* ''Die vier Species.'' (The four Species) Leipzig (1872) ([https://archive.org/details/dievierspecies00hessgoog Internet Archive])

His collected works were published in 1897 by [[Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities]].
